$comment: M2 additions to the build kit's M1 OpenAPI document. See contracts/README.md.

changes.why: The served contract is the kit's M1 document plus these changes; it needs its own version so a client can tell them apart.

changes.value: Generated from the build kit's M1 contract plus contracts/overlay.json. This is the Brand Consistency Scanner's API; the capability beneath it is the Consistency Engine, whose detector namespace is CE-. Implemented detectors: CE-LINK-01, CE-ASSET-01, CE-DATA-01, CE-MOBILE-01 (accepted also under their handoff names). Adds the M2 offer catalogue, the M3 requested-intake surface and protected report delivery, and the M4 engagement lifecycle. Operations under /public and /r have no authenticated actor and carry x-protected-by instead of x-minimum-role. Contract only; an operation appearing here is not a claim that a deployment serves it.
changes.why: The served contract now covers three detectors and four milestones' worth of surface. A reader should learn what is in it from the document rather than from a commit log.

CE-MOBILE-01 ships in this commit with its rule, its fixtures and its tests, so the enum it is requestable through moves with it. Its handoff spelling PDP-MOBILE-01 stays valid input. CE-CONTENT-01 and CE-VISUAL-01 stay unrequestable under either namespace: both turn on a category rubric that does not exist, and shipping them without one would assert taste as defect.

changes.value: Minimum role: operator. Phase: M1-M2. Membership, purpose, object and budget checks also apply. Detectors are limited to the implemented set — CE-LINK-01, CE-ASSET-01, CE-DATA-01 and CE-MOBILE-01 — and may be written in either the Consistency Engine namespace or the handoff's venture-scoped one; what is recorded is always the CE- id. Requesting CE-MOBILE-01 adds a second pair of captures at a phone viewport: the same page at another screen size, not an extra page. Contract only; not a claim this endpoint exists.

value.description: What the collector recorded about this observation: status, role classification, rendered outcome, timing. Only fields this system produced; never page content or scraped text.

changes.why: MF-ASSET-01 turns on facts the M1 Evidence shape had nowhere to carry: how an image was classified, and whether it actually painted. A reviewer cannot judge the claim without them, so they belong on the wire rather than only in the database.

Required rather than optional: an observation with no recorded detail is not evidence. This narrows a *response* schema, which is safe in a way narrowing a request schema would not be — the server always populates the field, and a client that ignores it is unaffected. generated-contract.test.ts enforces that distinction.

value.description: Detectors this deployment actually runs. The operator displays this rather than a constant compiled into its bundle, so the interface cannot claim a capability the server does not have.

changes.why: The workspace banner states which detectors are enabled. Deriving that from a value bundled into the client would let a stale bundle advertise a detector the server does not run; asking the server removes the possibility.

Required rather than optional: a session that does not say what the server runs would let the interface fall back to a guess. This narrows a response schema, which is safe — the server always populates it.

value.description: A commercial price in MINOR units of its currency. Deliberately not Money: Money carries provider cost in micro-units of the ledger currency, and the two must never be added. The differing field names make a mix-up a schema error rather than an arithmetic one.

Performs no business write: that the link was used is recorded as an append-only audit event, never as state a reader could change. Every failure — expired, revoked, mistyped, another workspace, never issued — returns the same 404. Contract only; not a claim this endpoint exists.

200.description: Successful operation. Does not imply a later workflow step completed.

404.description: This link is not valid. Returned identically for an expired link, a revoked one, a mistyped one, one belonging to another workspace, and one that never existed

changes.why: Issuing, listing and revoking a protected link are operator acts; reading through one is not, and has no actor at all. The public operation carries x-protected-by rather than x-minimum-role, and names the seven things that bound it. New operations only; every M1 call is untouched.

post.summary: Issue a protected link to a published report
post.description: Minimum role: reviewer. Phase: M3. Membership, purpose, object and budget checks also apply. Only a published report may be delivered, and the grant is bound to the version published at that moment. The response carries the token once and it cannot be retrieved again. Issuing a link sends nothing: delivery to the recipient is a separate act with a separate permission. Contract only; not a claim this endpoint exists.

get.summary: The report as a page, for the person it is about
get.description: No authentication. Server-rendered HTML with no script, outside the operator application because that sits behind Cloudflare Access in production and a customer must never need to get past Access to read their own report. Every failure — expired, revoked, mistyped, another workspace's, never issued — renders the same page, which says nothing about whether a report exists. Contract only; not a claim this endpoint exists.

200.description: The report page.

404.description: The same page for every kind of unusable link. Deliberately identical to a 200 in everything except status and content, so a prober learns nothing from either.

changes.why: The link an operator hands to a customer points here, so the contract has to describe it — and tests/contract/openapi-routes.test.ts requires every mounted route to be declared. It returns HTML rather than JSON, which is why it sits outside /public alongside the JSON form of the same grant.
Adds the customer-facing report page. Additive; no existing operation changed.

get.summary: The embeddable request form, as a script
get.description: No authentication. One script tag and one container element on a venture's own site. It derives the origin it posts to from its own URL rather than from an attribute, so an embedding page cannot point it at another workspace; it renders the channel's purpose text as text rather than supplying its own; and it writes into a Shadow DOM so neither it nor the host page can restyle the other. Contract only; not a claim this endpoint exists.

200.description: The script.

404.description: No such resource. Also returned when requested intake is switched off.

changes.why: The embed is a surface a stranger's browser fetches, so it belongs in the contract for the same reason the form and the report page do: tests/contract/openapi-routes.test.ts requires every mounted route to be declared, and an undeclared public surface is one nobody reviewed.
Adds the embeddable form script. Additive; no existing operation changed.
